newsitem.title: UK: Ldn palladium fixes at new recent high of $133.75.
newsitem.headline: Ldn palladium fixes at new recent high of $133.75.

text.p: Palladium was fixed a fresh recent high on Monday of $133.75 per ounce, up from $130.50 on Friday afternoon.
The fixing was its highest since July 13, 1996.
Dealers said palladium's strength continued to come from the stalled talks on Russia-Japan delivery contracts for 1997.
"Palladium is generally forecast to go higher because of the Russian export issue," a dealer said.
The lack of shipments from Russia, the world's leading supplier of the metal, has forced consumers into the dealer market to meet requirements and also encouraged speculator buying.
Palladium's main end-uses are in electronic components, autocatalysts which clean toxic gases out of car exhaust fumes and in dental alloys.
Budgetary and administrative problems have delayed the talks which would ususally have begun in December.
In North America the favoured sponge grade palladium has been commanding a higher than ususal premium over ingot grade reflecting increase production by the automotive industry.
